Subject: FinWave TTFT & streaming ops follow-up: pilot scope & next steps

Hi Alex / Marie —

Thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the TTFT + streaming pilot running next week: 

Summary of asks we captured:
- Target TTFT: P95 <= 200ms on shortest user prompts (goal: 150ms).
- Sustained throughput target: 150 req/s for initial pilot (burst up to 300 req/s).
- Concurrency per model instance: 16–32 tokens-in-flight target depending on model size.
- Streaming delivery: prefer SSE for browser clients; engineering may consider WebSocket if bi-directional state is needed.
- Chunk cadence: aim for chunking at ~120–250ms or ~300–500 token windows for predictable UX; we discussed adaptive chunking for longer responses.

What we (Redwood) will deliver this week:
1) A TTFT probe plan (attached) with request templates and load pattern.
2) A streaming chunking spec (attached) with example SSE frames and our recommended pacing.
3) An SDK snippet and curl examples to run the first probes against our sandbox.
4) Dashboard link and a short instrumentation checklist so you can see P50/P95/P99, tokens/sec, and chunk latency.

What we need from you:
- Sample payloads (3–5 real prompts) and expected average response length.
- Confirmation of client type (browser SSE vs mobile WebSocket) and whether you need partial-results deserialization.
- A contact on your platform team we can give sandbox access to (we'll use eng@finwave.io unless you prefer someone else).

Proposed timeline:
- Mon/Tue: exchange payloads and grant sandbox access.
- Wed–Thu: Redwood runs TTFT probes + streaming cadence experiments.
- Fri: debrief call to review P95 TTFT, chunk cadence, and recommended config (15–30 mins).

Next steps: can you confirm the two items we need (sample payloads + platform contact) by EOD Monday?

Thanks — looking forward to running the pilot.

Best,
Rishi

On Fri, Jan 16, 2026 at 11:03 AM Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finwave.io> wrote:
> One question: for the chunk cadence you listed 120–250ms — is that measured from last byte to last byte, or from server write intervals?

Great question — short answer: server write intervals.

More detail: Our recommended cadence window refers to how frequently the server flushes a chunk to the transport. That typically maps to a write every ~120–250ms under normal model generation rates, or when a chunk accumulates N tokens (we normally use a soft threshold, e.g., ~250–500 tokens for long responses). Browser rendering will generally display the chunk immediately once the event is received. To avoid very small fragments we use a minimum token threshold of ~30–50 tokens (or ~80ms) so clients don't get many tiny frames.

Fallbacks for TTFT spikes:
- Immediate: auto-fallback to a smaller model variant (compatible and validated) for degraded latency while preserving semantic fidelity.
- Near-term: switch to a warmed cache path for repeated prefixes (if applicable) to shave ~30–60ms.
- Long-term: recommend reserved concurrency or autoscale policy for production (we can help size it after the pilot).

We'll include these notes in the streaming_spec.pdf and the probe plan.

—Stephanie
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jan 19, 2026 at 09:05 AM Marie Kwan <mk@finwave.io> wrote:
> Two clarifications from our side:
> 1) We have an existing CDN in front of the app; will SSE streaming work reliably through that?
> 2) For fallback to smaller model variants, we need to preserve specific domain tokens (financial tickers). Can you confirm token-level consistency guarantees?

Hi Marie / Alex — quick answers below, we'll go deeper in the debrief Friday: 

1) CDN + SSE: Generally SSE works through CDNs if the CDN supports long-lived connections and passthrough of chunked responses. If your CDN terminates connections aggressively, WebSocket is an option (we can also recommend minimal config changes). We'll include a short CDN checklist in the drive link (headers to preserve, timeouts to increase).

2) Token-level consistency: When we fallback to a smaller variant we run a constrained sampling policy and a lightweight consistency check against critical tokens (we can pin token-lists — e.g., financial tickers — in the evaluation pipeline). That means we prioritize exact reproduction of a whitelist of tokens and bias sampling accordingly; not a 100% guarantee for arbitrary sequences but strong safeguards for critical tokens. We'll include a short test harness so you can validate fidelity on your samples.

Next steps I took: invited eng@finwave.io to the sandbox, uploaded the probe plan and streaming spec to the shared drive, and scheduled the debrief for Fri 16:00 ET (invite sent).

If you want, we can also run a short warmup today (5–10m) to demonstrate baseline TTFT on your sample prompts — tell us a time window and we'll do it.

Cheers,
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
